paper_metadata.title: Application of an upsampling algorithm to quantum state preparation of continuous and discrete probability distributions

experiments.description: State preparation of a univariate Gaussian probability distribution using the upsampling algorithm, converted to a quantum-forking circuit; demonstrated with n = 3 qubits.

algorithm.variant: upsampling-based quantum state preparation with quantum forking

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous PDF P(x|mu, sigma) is discretized on a sampling window of width w into 2^n points; amplitudes are proportional to square roots of sampled probabilities.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |psi_n> with amplitudes sqrt(P(x_n) delta_xn) for sampled Gaussian probabilities.

problem_instance.description: Univariate normal distribution state preparation example.

dataset_specification.description: Gaussian PDF P(x|mu, sigma) = (1/(sigma sqrt(2pi))) exp(-(x-mu)^2/(2 sigma^2)); capture centered at xbar = mu.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize the continuous PDF over a sampling window; use periodic extension and normalization factor delta_xn.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Sampling measurement shown in Fig. 4(a) from a quantum-forking circuit converted from an n = 3 upsampling circuit.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute rotation angles from the Gaussian PDF and convert the divide-and-conquer upsampling circuit to a quantum-forking circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Project measurement outcomes to obtain sampled Gaussian probabilities.

speedup_claims.factor: polylogarithmic gate depth vs exponential gate depth
speedup_claims.conditions: after conversion to quantum forking; with d = 2^n - 1
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is asymptotic and circuit-depth based; no runtime benchmark or classical Monte Carlo baseline is reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Exponential gate depth for the divide-and-conquer circuit; polylogarithmic gate depth after quantum forking, stated as O(log2^2(d)) with d = 2^n - 1.

experiments.description: State preparation of a lognormal distribution via mapping from a Gaussian distribution, using the same upsampling framework.

algorithm.variant: upsampling-based quantum state preparation with quantum forking

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Continuous lognormal PDF is mapped to a Gaussian in x = log y; sampled points are y_n = exp(x_n) with widths delta_y_n = exp(x_n) delta_x_n.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare amplitudes corresponding to sampled lognormal probabilities.

problem_instance.description: Lognormal distribution example derived from Gaussian mapping.

dataset_specification.description: P(y|mu, sigma) = (1/(y sigma sqrt(2pi))) exp(-(log y - mu)^2/(2 sigma^2)); support on 0 <= y < infinity.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Apply logarithmic change of variables x = log y, then discretize y_n = exp(x_n) and scale widths by delta_y_n = exp(x_n) delta_x_n.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Described analytically; no separate numerical run details reported.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Map lognormal distribution to Gaussian via x = log y and discretize the transformed variable.

speedup_claims.factor: exponential gate depth before quantum forking; polylogarithmic after conversion
speedup_claims.caveats: No separate numerical run details are reported for the lognormal case.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Same as the underlying upsampling state-preparation method; exponential gate depth before quantum forking and polylogarithmic after conversion.

experiments.description: State preparation of a binomial discrete probability distribution using the discrete-probability extension of the upsampling algorithm; demonstrated with n = 4 qubits.

algorithm.variant: upsampling-based discrete probability state preparation with quantum forking

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discrete probabilities P(k,l) are loaded into amplitudes sqrt(P(k,l)); the paper derives an auxiliary complementary-probability state to make the circuit compatible with the upsampling construction.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |psi_n> whose amplitudes are square roots of binomial probabilities.

dataset_specification.description: P(k,l) = (l choose k) p^k q^(l-k), with k in {0,1,...,l} and p+q=1.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Construct discrete probabilities and use the discrete-probability version of the upsampling algorithm; the figure shows projection of the |0> state of the most significant qubit.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Sampling/measurement plot shown in Fig. 6(a) from a quantum-forking circuit converted from an n = 4 upsampling circuit.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute discrete binomial probabilities and derive the corresponding rotation angles for the discrete-probability state-preparation circuit.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Project measurement outcomes to obtain the binomial distribution.

speedup_claims.factor: polylogarithmic gate depth vs exponential gate depth
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a projected asymptotic improvement, not a measured runtime speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Exponential gate depth for the divide-and-conquer circuit; polylogarithmic gate depth after quantum forking, stated as O(log2^2(d)) with d = 2^n - 1.
